original.target_description: Published article, Study 1: Cornell introductory psychology undergraduates rated their ability in driving a car relative to classmates on a percentile scale; target comparison is mean comparative percentile against 50 (average), not the regressions predicting percentile judgments.

n.sample_role: Participants contributing to the Study 1 Table 2 comparative ability estimate; table-specific N, not the separate pretest sample.
n.exclusions: No target-test exclusions or missing observations documented; Table 2 explicitly labels Study 1 N = 37. The n = 19 experience-only follow-up in footnote 3 is a different pooled analysis.
n.location: p. 224, Table 2 title; p. 223, Study 1 Method, Participants

es.location: p. 224, Table 2, Driving row, Percentile estimate column and table notes

p.location: p. 224, Table 2, Driving row, Percentile estimate column and significance legend; Study 1 Results, Above- and below-average effects

replication.target_description: Study 1, original replication condition; Driving comparative ability versus scale midpoint; one-sample Wilcoxon test of median comparative ability.

n.sample_role: Participants in the original replication condition after exclusions; condition sample, used for item-wise comparative ability analyses.
n.exclusions: 65 of 756 participants excluded across all conditions, leaving 691; condition-specific excluded counts not supplied here. Criteria: English proficiency, seriousness, hypothesis awareness, prior exposure, incomplete responses, and US origin.
n.location: Main text p.48, Table 15.3, Replication condition header; p.21 Participants and power analyses; supplementary pp.3–4 exclusion criteria

es.location: Supplementary p.18, Table 8.1, Driving row, Effect size r column

p.location: Supplementary p.18, Table 8.1, Driving row, P-value column

reported_success.location: Main text pp.45–46, above/below average effects discussion; p.48 Table 15.3, Driving row
reported_success.quote: Using both one-sample Wilcoxon and t-tests, both above-and-below-average effects replicated with smaller effects

notes:
No detailed locator supplied; neutral outcome and Study 1 identify the original replication condition. Chose the authors' explicitly printed Wilcoxon r and its accompanying p from the same table/test; did not convert the separately reported t-test Cohen's d. Narrative replication verdict covers both Wilcoxon and t-tests; item-specific t-test comparison is labelled Signal - consistent, smaller. Original full text unavailable: DOI access failed, publisher PDF returned 403, OpenAlex and Unpaywall returned no OA location, and author homepage returned 403. Original statistics recapitulated in the replication supplement were not substituted for the original primary paper.
Source follow-up: Target side only. Source identifies the published Kruger (1999) article and the supplied title. Table 2 prints a mean comparative percentile of 65.4, with significance for comparison against 50. No r or target-specific t statistic is printed for this test, so es.value is null and no conversion is performed. The Own ability and Peers’ ability columns are standardized regression betas for different tests and are not effect sizes for the target above-average comparison. The table footnote has an OCR artifact in the four-star p label; it prints the bound < .0001. Replication and reported success are unassigned placeholders.
